Drivers Not Receiving Route Assignments

8 min read Updated May 22, 2025 iOS & Android

When you dispatch a route, drivers should receive a push notification and see the route load in their app within about 30 seconds. If that's not happening, this guide covers every known cause in order of likelihood.

Symptoms

This article applies if you're experiencing any of the following:

  • Dispatched a route but the driver received no notification
  • The route shows as "Dispatched" in the dashboard but is missing from the driver's app
  • Driver says they received a notification but tapping it didn't open the route
  • Routes appear in the driver's app hours later, with a delay
Before you start

Check the Route Activity Log in your dispatcher dashboard (Routes → select route → Activity tab). It will show whether the route was sent and whether the delivery server acknowledged receipt. This narrows the problem to either our servers or the driver's device.

Quick Checklist

Run through these first — they resolve the majority of cases:

1. Notification Permissions Are Blocked

This is the most common cause. If a driver denies notification permissions on first launch — or if system updates have reset them — PocketRoute can't deliver route alerts.

Check on iOS

  1. Open Settings on the driver's iPhone
  2. Scroll to PocketRoute
  3. Tap Notifications
  4. Ensure Allow Notifications is on, and that Alerts and Sounds are enabled

Check on Android

  1. Open Settings → Apps → PocketRoute
  2. Tap Notifications
  3. Ensure the Route Assignments and Dispatch Alerts channels are both enabled
Android Battery Optimization

On many Android manufacturers (Samsung, Xiaomi, OnePlus), aggressive battery optimization kills background processes and blocks notifications. Go to Settings → Battery → Battery Optimization and set PocketRoute to Unrestricted or Don't optimize.

2. Driver Is Not Signed In

Push tokens are only registered while a driver is signed in. If they signed out (or were signed out by a session expiry), they won't receive notifications.

Have the driver open the app and confirm they see their name in Settings → Account. If the sign-in screen is showing, they need to re-authenticate. After signing in, wait 60 seconds and re-dispatch the route — the push token will re-register automatically.

What the driver sees What it means Fix
Sign-in screen on open Session expired or manually signed out Sign in again, re-dispatch
Wrong name in Account settings Multiple accounts on one device Sign out, sign in with correct account
Correct name, no routes Route not yet synced or dispatch failed Pull to refresh on Routes tab
Route visible but no notification Push delivery failed; route still synced Check notification permissions (see above)

3. App Was Force-Quit or Restricted (iOS)

iOS can restrict an app's ability to receive push notifications if the device is in Low Power Mode, or if the user has recently force-closed the app by swiping up from the app switcher.

While PocketRoute doesn't require the app to be open to receive notifications, iOS occasionally throttles push delivery after force-quit. The fix:

1

Disable Low Power Mode on the driver's iPhone

Settings → Battery → Low Power Mode → Off. Low Power Mode suppresses background network requests and delays push delivery by up to 30 minutes.

2

Open PocketRoute once

Have the driver launch the app and leave it in the background (don't force-quit). iOS will restore full push delivery priority within 60 seconds.

3

Re-dispatch the route

In your dashboard, open the route → Actions → Resend to Driver. This sends a fresh push notification.

4. Route Was Not Actually Dispatched

It's possible the route was saved as a draft rather than dispatched. Check in the dashboard:

  • Routes in Draft status have not been sent to any driver
  • Routes in Assigned status are assigned but awaiting dispatch
  • Routes in Dispatched status have been sent — check the Activity Log for delivery confirmation

If the route shows as Draft or Assigned, click Dispatch Now on the route detail page.

5. Push Notification Delivery Delay

In rare cases, Apple (APNS) or Google (FCM) push infrastructure experiences delays — usually during high-traffic periods like early morning delivery windows. If the Activity Log shows "Delivered to push provider" but the driver hasn't received it, this is likely the cause.

Workarounds:

  • Have the driver pull to refresh on the Routes tab — the route will load even without the notification, since routes also sync on a 60-second background interval
  • Send the driver a direct message or call to tell them the route is ready
  • Use Actions → Resend to Driver to attempt another push delivery
Push Delivery Status

PocketRoute logs whether our server successfully handed the notification to Apple/Google. We don't have visibility into final device delivery — that's controlled by APNS/FCM. Check status.pocketroute.io if you suspect a widespread issue.

Still Stuck?

If none of the above resolves the issue, our support team can review your account's push delivery logs directly. Please include:

  • The Route ID (found in the route URL: app.pocketroute.io/routes/r_xxxx)
  • The driver's account email
  • Device model and OS version
  • Approximate time you dispatched the route
